SKYLINEwingsuit flight simulator

Real aerodynamics, real gravity, real air. Ten lines from the Alps to the Himalaya, through a city of skyscrapers and a Highland glen — and one over Cambourne Village College. Fly the gates on your own, or race computer pilots to the finish.

Keyboard, mouse, gamepad or touch. Best with headphones.

Short challenges with stars and personal bests. Pick one, then pick a map.

How to fly

Controls

W↑Dive — lower angle of attack, gain speed
S↓Flare — raise angle of attack (canopy: both brakes)
ADRoll / bank to turn (canopy: toggles)
QELeg yaw (subtle)
ShiftTuck arms — faster, worse glide
SpaceJump • deploy parachute • ski mode after a snow stall
B T UFire Booster • Slow-Mo • Updraft (loaded at checkpoints)
CCamera: chase, helmet, trackside, drone
R / Shift RCheckpoint respawn / restart line
V H MSmoke • HUD • mute
EscPause
Right-dragLook around
Hold EnterFast-forward under canopy

Gamepad: left stick flies, A jumps/deploys, Y camera, LT flare, RT tuck, right stick looks. Touch: left thumb stick and on-screen buttons (change the layout, size and tilt steering in Settings → Controls).

Flying like a pro

  • Arcade or Realistic? Arcade starts you in the air with big rainbow gates, coins, bonus rings and a gentle push; crash and you are back at the last gate in a second. Realistic is the full simulator with the exit, canopy and landing.
  • Race. Race up to 5 computer pilots (Easy, Medium or Hard) on any map. Everyone jumps on GO; the first through the finish gate wins (each missed gate adds 3 s), then land in the circle. The rivals run on your device — there are no real people and nothing goes online.
  • Tight gaps. In Metro Heights and Highland Glen some gates sit in narrow gaps — between towers, under a sky bridge, through a hole in a skyscraper, under power lines, through a viaduct arch or between wind-turbine blades. Those gates stay small even in Arcade: line up early and fly straight through.
  • The exit. You start with no airspeed. Fall for a few seconds, then pull gently on S to pressurise the suit and round out into flight.
  • Energy is everything. Dive to trade height for speed, flare to trade speed for height. A flare from 250 km/h can buy you a 40 m climb.
  • Glide ratio. Your suit glides 2.2–3.1 m forward per metre of height. Gates sit on a line you can make — if you sink below them, you can’t climb back.
  • Proximity. Fly close to rock, trees and water for combo points that multiply over time. Crash and you lose the unbanked combo.
  • Stall. Too much angle of attack and the suit stops flying: lift drops, a wing can drop. Push forward to recover.
  • Thin air. In the Himalaya the air is half as dense — you fly 40% faster, controls feel loose, the canopy lands hot.
  • Canopy. Deploy above 200 m. It takes ~3 s and ~60 m to open. Land into the wind (watch the windsock) and flare at 3–4 m.
  • Coins & Locker. Every checkpoint pays coins, and big scores and medals pay more. Spend them in the Locker on outfits and power-ups. Power-ups load when you pass a checkpoint: Booster, Slow-Mo and Updraft you fire yourself; Second Life, Shield, Gate Magnet and Coin Doubler work on their own.
  • Himalaya skis. Hit the snow at any speed — in your wingsuit or under your parachute — and your skis click on. Tuck (W) to build speed and hit an orange ramp at 80 km/h or more to be launched back into the air, or ski into the target circle and stop to finish.
  • Volcano. The crater throws glowing lava bombs. Most miss you — a close dodge earns style points.

Settings

Quality changes apply the next time you load a line.

Tilt steering uses the motion sensor. On iPad and iPhone Safari asks for permission the first time.

Silent mode is also the speaker button in the corner of the title screen, and the M key.

Your save

Your coins, outfits, medals and settings save automatically on this device.
